description: A principal must approve and finalize an eighth-grade makerspace program, including enrollment, supervision, materials, and digital-design procedures, with input from the STEM teacher, school nurse, and technology coordinator.

shared_context.S1: The school is preparing an eighth-grade makerspace program using soldering stations, hand tools, and a laser cutter.
shared_context.S2: The draft program proposes 24 students, one STEM teacher supervising, standard metal components, and cloud-based computer-aided design files.
shared_context.S3: The program is scheduled to meet twice each week during the spring semester.
shared_context.S4: Dr. Morgan makes the final authorization decision and follows the school's routine practice of asking the STEM teacher, school nurse, and technology coordinator for relevant implementation information before approving a new program.

PF1.text: Ms. Rivera's completed room-safety review found that the makerspace may enroll no more than 16 students, and any session using soldering stations with more than 12 students requires two supervising adults; she completed the review this week, but the draft program form still shows the original staffing and enrollment numbers.

PF2.text: Nurse Brooks's review of the participating students' health records found one student with a documented severe nickel allergy; that student may participate only when the program uses nickel-free components and the nurse has approved the materials list before each session, and the health-record review has not yet been added to the program file.

PF3.text: Mr. Chen confirmed with the district technology office that student design files for this equipment may not use cloud storage; the approved workflow is an offline design workstation with files transferred by encrypted USB after an IT malware scan, but he has not yet replaced the cloud-storage instruction in the draft.

acceptance_conditions: Enrollment must be capped at 16 students.
Soldering sessions with the approved enrollment must have two supervising adults.
The program must use nickel-free components.
A nurse materials-approval commitment must be recorded.
Design files must use an offline workstation and encrypted USB transfer.
An IT malware-scan commitment must be recorded.

content_checks.C4: 'approve' in decisions['materials_policy'] and 'before each session' in decisions['materials_policy']
content_checks.C5: 'offline' in decisions['design_file_method'] and 'encrypted USB' in decisions['design_file_method']

decisive_facts.why: The room-safety review changes enrollment from the draft 24 students to exactly 16 and changes soldering supervision to two supervising adults when more than 12 students are present.
The student's documented nickel allergy changes the materials policy to nickel-free components and requires Nurse Brooks to approve the materials list before each session.
The district technology confirmation changes file handling from cloud storage to an offline workstation with encrypted USB transfer after an IT malware scan.
